findings.documented: Append the API key as an api_key query parameter on every request.
findings.actual: The server returns HTTP 401 with message 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter.' The key must be sent as a header.
findings.how_found: First request using the documented query-param style returned 401 with that exact message.
findings.impact: Every request in the documented style fails authentication entirely.

findings.documented: Response contains field 'token', expires_in: 86400 (24 hours). 'There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: Response contains 'access_token' (not 'token'), expires_in: 900 (15 minutes), plus 'refresh_token' and 'refresh_url: /auth/refresh'. A refresh flow exists.
findings.how_found: Inspected the raw login response body. expires_in was 900, not 86400. refresh_token and refresh_url fields were present.
findings.impact: Sessions documented as lasting 24h actually expire in 15 minutes. Apps not implementing the undocumented refresh flow will stop working mid-session.

findings.documented: Not documented. Docs explicitly state 'There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh accepts {refresh_token: <token>} and returns a new access_token. This endpoint exists and works.
findings.how_found: Found refresh_url field in the login response pointing to /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: Developers reading only the docs would not know to implement token refresh and their sessions would expire after 15 minutes.

findings.documented: Maximum limit is 200. Response shape: {total, page, page_size, results}.
findings.actual: Maximum limit enforced is 50 — sending limit=200 returns only 50 records. Response shape: {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results}. Fields 'page' and 'page_size' do not appear.
findings.how_found: Sent GET /v1/listings?limit=200 and received a response with 'count':50 and 'limit':50, with has_more:true.
findings.impact: Code relying on the documented 200-record limit would page incorrectly and miss data. Code expecting page/page_size fields would break.

findings.documented: Returns only active listings. 'Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.'
findings.actual: The response includes listings where is_live is false — inactive listings are returned alongside active ones.
findings.how_found: Counted listings with is_live=false in the full retrieved dataset; found records with is_live:false in /v1/listings.
findings.impact: Apps trusting the docs would show inactive listings to users without filtering them out.

findings.documented: Returns pre-computed aggregates: city, total_listings, median_price, median_price_per_sqft, by_locality, by_bhk.
findings.actual: Returns HTTP 404 with {"detail": "Not Found"}. The endpoint is not implemented.
findings.impact: Any dashboard or insights screen relying on this endpoint receives no data.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites returns saved listings for the logged-in user. POST /v1/favourites adds a listing. DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} removes one.
findings.actual: All requests to /v1/favourites return HTTP 404. The endpoint is not implemented.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/favourites with a valid Bearer token; received 404.
findings.impact: Saved-listings feature cannot use the API; must fall back to client-side storage.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees (integer).
findings.actual: Observed values like 80.0, 38.5, 3.22 — these are clearly lakhs (×100,000), not rupees. A value of 3.22 in rupees would make no sense for a property project.
findings.how_found: Compared price_min/price_max values in /v1/projects responses with prices in /v1/listings for the same properties. Project prices were ~100,000x smaller than expected.
findings.impact: Displaying raw price_min/price_max as rupees shows wildly incorrect prices. Must multiply by 100,000 (1 lakh) before display.

findings.documented: total_listings 'is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.'
findings.actual: Many projects report a total_listings that does not match the actual count of listings with that project_id in the retrievable /v1/listings dataset.
findings.how_found: Fetched all listings and all projects, grouped listings by project_id, and compared counts to each project's reported total_listings.
findings.impact: total_listings cannot be trusted as a count of current listings. Users and apps relying on it will see wrong numbers.

findings.documented: Every listing in /v1/listings should be individually retrievable via /v1/listing/{id}.
findings.actual: HTTP 404 returned for ZER-3003685: "Not Found". The ID appears normally in /v1/listings but 404s on the individual endpoint.
findings.how_found: Clicked a listing row; the detail page 404d. Confirmed via the ghost-listing probe on the Insights screen.
findings.impact: Detail pages for these listings are broken. May indicate phantom records in the collection index.
